A few thoughts...

1. I think it's critical we never purge anything that's not yet replicated. I'm not sure what the best way to achieve this is. You could check the changes feed for the last updated date for this doc and compare that to the last sync time. Alternatively you could listen for dbsync to complete and then prompt Purger to check.
2. Seeing as you're doing this on refresh consider doing it in the bootstrap layer so the UI is blocked (nice spinner, "purging docs" message, etc). This would mean the whole process can run faster because angular wouldn't be constantly updating the UI as docs are purged.
3. We set auto compaction on in PouchDB but it would be worth considering an explicit compaction after deletion. This is a slow process but IIRC until compaction you don't see improvements in performance or disk space and I don't completely trust auto compaction to keep working. 
4. If the doc is updated on the server it'll conflict on replication. I'm guessing that'll be silently ignored which is probably the right thing to do in this case, but we could consider bringing the doc back?

There are a couple of reasons we don't (rather didn't) limit the changes feed:

1. Pre 3.0 - Because we would batch the requests made to CouchDB with 100 `doc_ids` to take advantage of the optimizations done to that path in Couch 1.x, then we would merge the results and return everything. Together with the fact that seq-s cannot be reliably compared and sorted, it would have been impossible to generate a correct last_seq to return. 
2. Post 3.0 - Because when querying with `_doc_ids` filter and `limit`, the `last_seq` returned was not reliable (when doing next queries following received last_seq, many changes were skipped). 
**NB** I have tested and found this bug on Couch 1.x, Couch 2.0, Couch 2.1 and Couch 2.2.
**It appears to have been fixed in Couch 2.3 !! :tada:**

I will run some more tests in Couch 2.3 to make extra sure that last_seq's are indeed reliable, if they are, there are no impediments into returning batched changes!

From a data architecture perspective, this ended up being implemented as follows.

When a mute or unmute form (`data_record`) is submitted, this will update the appropriate place/person records in the `medic` DB ***and*** the corresponding `-info` record in the `medic-sentinel` database.  The updates are done as follows:

## medic DB 

- A`muted` field is added whenever a *person* or *place* record is ***muted***
- The value of the `muted` field will be the timestamp of when the person/place was muted
- The timestamp used is when the sentinel transition was run on this document (ie when the muting/unmuting form was *synced*), ***NOT*** the timestamp of when the form was *submitted*.
- If an already muted person or place is muted again, nothing is updated.  The `muted` field will retain the original timestamp
- When *person* or *places* are ***unmuted***, the `muted` field is completely removed
- This applies to the following document types `person`, `clinic`, `health_center`, `district_hospital`
- To check (in SQL) whether or not a person/place is muted, you can simply use `doc ? 'muted'`, this checks the existence of a key in JSON.  If the key does not exist, `doc ? 'muted'` will evaluate to `false`

#### Example of a muted `health_center`
```
{
  "_id": "8d2e5384-0421-45ea-9cba-6adf09d5296f",
  "_rev": "11-58ec8cb4a26de08bd12ea1ba80446a35",
  "parent": {
    "_id": "45cc55c5-302d-49ce-8edf-fe77a8e0f110"
  },
  "name": "Red Foreman Area",
  "geolocation": "",
  "contact": {
    "_id": "ef0d26b8-bf27-41f3-a9ac-f7613238b0c3",
    "parent": {
      "_id": "8d2e5384-0421-45ea-9cba-6adf09d5296f",
      "parent": {
        "_id": "45cc55c5-302d-49ce-8edf-fe77a8e0f110"
      }
    }
  },
  "type": "health_center",
  "reported_date": 1542228245476,
  "muted": "2018-12-03T15:36:08.639Z"
}
```

## medic-sentinel DB
The muting history for a person/place is accessible from the corresponding `info` document stored in the `medic-sentinel` DB.

- When a person/place is first muted, the `muting_history` key will be added
- The value of this key is an array of mute/unmute activities
- Each array element will include (1) whether it was muted or unmuted; (2) timestamp of when the activity occurred; and (3) the `data_record` that caused this record to be muted or unmuted.
- The timestamp used is when the sentinel transition was run on this document (ie when the muting/unmuting form was *synced*), ***NOT*** the timestamp of when the form was *submitted*.
- Like the docs in the `medic` DB, if the person/place is already muted, muting them again will not add or update anything in the `muting_history`.  The same is true for unmuting.

#### Example muting history stored on the `info` doc

```
{
  "_id": "8d2e5384-0421-45ea-9cba-6adf09d5296f-info",
  "_rev": "20-14c194aa7f039a72aee3367d4d778cbd",
  "type": "info",
  "doc_id": "8d2e5384-0421-45ea-9cba-6adf09d5296f",
  "initial_replication_date": "2018-11-14T20:44:05.657Z",
  "latest_replication_date": "2018-12-03T15:36:10.617Z",
  "transitions": {},
  "muting_history": [
    {
      "muted": true,
      "date": "2018-11-29T14:31:57.250Z",
      "report_id": "7e09d2fb-0561-4806-84f7-0d362b959827"
    },
    {
      "muted": false,
      "date": "2018-11-29T21:47:07.020Z",

To fix, I'm changing
`query({ silent: true, limit: liveList.count() });`
to
`query({ silent: true, limit: Math.max(50, liveList.count()) });`

In the case of this test failure, the list length was 0 so no items could be inserted. The test failed when run as part of the suite because the previous test ended on the Reports page - so the page was updated via Changes. This did not repro when the test was run individually because the page was updated through other code paths. The bug did not previously manifest because of `options.limit = options.limit || 50;` which handles the case properly for lists of length 0 only.

The issue has been marked as a bug [by CouchDB folk](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/1810) and resolving it requires updating a CouchDB dependency (`mochiweb`).

We can work around it by changing CouchDB configuration, specifically:

```
[chttpd]
server_options = [{recbuf, undefined}]    
		|
		V
server_options = [{recbuf, some_positive_integer}]
```

The value we should choose is up for debate, more details about what `recbuf` is can be found [here](http://erlang.org/doc/man/inet.html#getopts-2).
[This](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/1409) is the original issue that caused this change. I'm unaware if we've had problems of the sort. 
Pre CouchDB 2.3.0, this value was defaulted to `262144` and it was part of `chttpd.socket_options`:
```
[chttpd]
socket_options = [{recbuf, 262144}, {sndbuf, 262144}, {nodelay, true}]
```

I've created a [PR #5105](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/pull/5105) to demo the fact that adding the config fixes the issue.

> If each usage can be replaced in a nice way make those changes and disable the Changes service for online users.

Just an idea -- but if these can be solved for online users, why not remove this code and make these changes for all users? Keeping it for only select users may further increase code complexity and test scenarios.  

Here are supporting anecdotes as to how these same changes may also benefit offline users:

* Given a scenario where the user goes to contacts tab > selects a contact > edits the contact. We are three screens deep and still processing, requerying, and redrawing changes on both hidden screens. Since this happens in parallel, it can impact the performance of the user's active tasks unnecessarily.
* The logic we have when a change occurs is often similar to "requery and redraw everything." In some cases, this may result in multiple seconds of high resource consumption (battery life) - many times with no resulting UI change.
* If you sync a bunch of contact changes while the contacts tab is open, the contact tab is constantly requerying and redrawing until the sync completes. I have no hard data, but it seems very possible this could negatively impact the sync.
As this bug can be avoided by changing CouchDB configuration, I've opened an issue in `medic-infrastructure`.

Supervisors are in a grey area where they pull quite a lot so it may make sense at this level.

The problem described above by @newtnewt is not related to the original problem reported by the issue.
Instead it is caused by 3 things:
1. a folder structure + ddoc rewrite path changes that were done in 3.0 that are causing our manifest to move from `/static/dist/manifest.appcache` to `/manifest.appcache`
2. How application cache works and the fact that we are not registering a listener for the `obsolete` AppCache event
3. receiving the changes that would trigger the AppCache to be updated in very quick succession 

What happens is: 
 - Webapp receives an `appcache` or/and `_design/medic-client` change, which calls `applicationCache.update()`.
 - The browser tries to get the appcache.manifest file and gets a 404. 
 - This doesn't throw an error (that we try to catch) and doesn't fire an `error` event that we listen to, instead it fires an `obsolete` event that we don't listen to - hence no update prompt.
 
Side events: 
 - The `obsolete` event does INVALIDATE the cache, so on next reload the new resources are downloaded.
 - When multiple `applicationCache.update()` calls are done in quick succession, they are debounced with the immediate style (if one request is pending, the next ones do nothing), so effectively one request is executed.
 - if the 2 changes that trigger the cache update (ddoc and appcache) are received in quick succession, only one would effectively update appcache (one request + one obsolete event).
 - In the cases when the 2 changes that trigger appcache update are received separately, the first one would trigger the obsolete event while the second one would throw an error (there is no appcache to update at this point, it had been invalidated by the obsolete event before) that we catch successfully and show the prompt.
 This is why I was not seeing this in my tests, my `appcache` and `_design/medic-client` changes were farther apart and thus triggered 2 appcache updates instead if just one, like Nick was seeing in his tests.
 - if replicated and not reloaded, the app is unusable due to the code expecting permissions to exist in `medic-client` ddoc

The CHT only supports the exporting of a dataValueSet which does not reference a `name`.

> As to whether this should bring API down, that's an interesting question.

imo Invalid configurations shouldn't crash the API.  If an app builder does somehow upload an invalid configuration like this, it's a poor experience with a high burden of education/diagnosis to investigate via docker/couchdb. Currently, App Builders have to:

1. bash into docker
1. read through the logs
1. understand the log output enough to know which config component specifically is causing the problem (in this case, not straightforward)
1. establish a connection to the database
1. delete or alter the configuration directly in couchdb

The ideal App Builder experience would be via medic-conf, which requires a running API.
If this happens on a dev instance (or even in production), SRE would become involved to resolve the issue.

Ex:
```
{
  "replication_depth": [
    { "role": "district_manager", "depth": 1 },
    { "role": "national_manager", "depth": 2, "report_depth": 1 }
  ]
}
```

In terms of what is visible, for example for 
`{ "role": "national_manager", "depth": 2, "report_depth": 1 }`, a hierarchy like `district (0) > center (1) > clinic (2) > area (3)` and a supervisor at `district` level. 

This supervisor would see `district`, `center` and `clinic`, along with any other person that belongs to `district` and `center`. 
The supervisor would not see any person belonging to `clinic` and no `area`s. 
The `report_depth` of 1, in this case, would mean that this supervisor can only see reports of `district` (0) and `center` (1) level, and no reports at `clinic` level, unless they're submitted by himself! 

If you set `report_depth` to be larger than `depth`, it would have no effect. 
Also, without the `depth` setting, it would have no effect (`{ "role": "district_manager", "report_depth": 1 }` is ignored)

This differs from the existing concept because it's not information about the current user. Because of how our menu works and the multiple states that a header icon has (inactive, hovered, and active), there's a downside in allowing "any icon that conforms to the specs" to be a header icon. 

We allow `.png` and `.svg` images as icons. 

There are ways that we can apply an overlay over a png image to change its color, but these are not widely supported by browsers. If we allow png icons as header icons, they will be a static color without any hover/active effects. 

My initial thought was to filter out resource icons to the ones that are in svg format when selecting a header icon, but we can allow any icon with the above caveat.

As Max said we're making this simpler for the 3.10.0 implementation...

1. When creating users the admin should have the option of providing a password (as they do now), _or_ sending a magic link via SMS.
2. If they pick magic link then we generate a random complex password with a 24 hour expiry.
3. Then we send a configurable SMS message containing a link to that project's instance with the credentials hashed and we forget the password. NB: Hashing is not secure, and the SMS is not encrypted.
4. The user clicks the link. If the app is installed it will open the app (that's the magic part). If it's not installed open in a browser. The default SMS message should encourage users to go to the app store and download the app first.
5. The login page detects the hashed credentials and changes the password to a new random password which nobody knows, and then logs the user in, with no user interaction whatsoever.

Password recovery:
1. The user contacts the IT administrator
2. The IT administrator either updates the user to have a configured password, or clicks a "regenerate password" button which generates a new temporary password, sends the magic link to the user, and so on as above.

Notes:
- The SMS option will not work for users who want to use multiple devices - they should use the configured password option
- The SMS option will not work for multiple users on one device - they should use the configured password option. The admin app should ensure the user's phone number is unique before sending the SMS.
- Anyone with access to the device will be able to access the app
- The user should not be able to log out easily because they will not be able to log in again
- Password recovery is a manual process

I...I think I found the problem?  I think I found the problem!! Our forms are structured to use the implicit relationship of a `label` tag by virtue of it wrapping around in `input` tag (as opposed to using the explicit `for="ID_HERE"` syntax). This is all fine and dandy, except that there's not one, but *two* `input`s inside the `label` tag in question.

If I go in via the developer tools and delete the first one (which is invisible `display: none`) then when I click the label the wrong behavior goes away and the correct behavior is seen. w00t!  This is the `intput` tag that's causing the problem in the rendered DOM: 

```html
<input type="date" name="/data/contact/ephemeral_dob/dob_calendar" data-required="true()" data-constraint="floor(decimal-date-time(.)) <= floor(decimal-date-time(today()))" data-relevant="not(selected(../dob_method,'approx'))" data-type-xml="date" style="display: none;">
```

Ah! And I found a possible fix.  It appears that the `label` tag is binding ("binding"?) to the *first* `input` inside it.  In our problem case, it's this invisible input mentioned above. Re-ordering the DOM so that this  `input` is rendered after the "real" one (though it looks like it's actually the fake one), the problem goes away.  

How easy this is to do is another question ;)

Final thoughts: I was trying to preload the resources which the service worker loads in the worker route, and noticed that even if I try to invalidate the preload intentionally (to debug), the browser isn’t giving any error or warning, perhaps because it's background process ( 🤔 ? ) Learned that this service worker is autogenerated by using sw-precache, which is obsolete and now it’s called Workbox… The Creator doesn’t motivate the usage of preload if we are already using precache: https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache/issues/259 Learning about Workbox… it has a feature that already make the preload mechanism if the browser supports it, but they suggest not to use it if the app is App Shell design with cached HTML, since it won’t give much benefit : https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/modules/workbox-navigation-preload However, it could still have a little benefit in the first load on very slow connections while combining with HTTP/2, this needs to be tested. It was decided to log an [issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6514) to upgrade from sw-precache to Workbox and while on it, enable the Workbox's preload feature and test. This issue's PR will submit the preload of login's CSS and JS only.

moment.js is stable and hasn't changed significantly recently which makes this tempting.

The fact that they follow semver doesn't help here as core upgrading would still add upgrade burden because there's no way for core to know if the configuration will break or not. Furthermore it would force us to make a major release to properly communicate the broken backwards compatibility. This would be even worse if core decided to migrate from moment to another library, as we just did for underscore to lodash. It's important that core is free to make this sorts of changes and test that it's backwards compatible so our partners have the confidence to upgrade frequently.

Exposing moment on `utils.moment` has the same issues.

One more thing to consider is are there other libraries that would be useful? I suspect moment.js is the _most_ useful but I imagine there are other libraries that may be useful from time to time.

> What do you think of this proposed plan to get rid of nools in core and add it as an optional dependency in medic-conf? This hopefully mitigates your long-term concerns.

I think this solves all my concerns. If there's a way to include any library you like in the compiled code then the library and version chosen can be completely independent of any library and version that the core deployment has. The main downside to this approach is the moment library would be included in _both_ the bundled app and the bundled config. I think this can be mitigated sufficiently by making sure tree shaking is working in the built config so unused library functions are discarded.

Latest iteration is to have 2 levels of priority for MVP, labelling high priority items as "Priority Care", visible across the app and including a card on the contact pages. The concept here is to simplify the identification for priority items without losing the indication of person or task type by including a coloured bounding box for each icon. This is also clearer than simply adding a conditional icon (ex. shield) as by only using 2 colours a user can easily scan for important tasks. Additionally I'd propose to use a single colour for active tabs to not confuse additional colours with other meanings.

I think it looks great. It leads me to these proposed assumptions and questions:

**Assumptions**
- Conceptually, this new design caters to two levels of priority: priority and non-priority (not sure of best terminology)
- There are three entities that might have a priority associated to them: families, family members, and tasks
- Tasks associated to a priority family can be priority or non-priority
- Tasks associated to a non-priority family can be priority or non-priority
- Tasks associated to a priority person can be priority or non-priority
- Tasks associated to a non-priority person can be priority or non-priority
- Tasks associated to a person can be priority or non-priority regardless of that person’s family’s priority
- Other places and/or place contacts higher in the hierarchy do not require priority (at this time)
- Tasks associated to places/place contacts higher in the hierarchy can still be considered priority or non-priority (using existing functionality)
- Existing Task functionality caters to two levels of task priority, high and medium
- Existing Task functionality allows you to conditionally identify that task as being high risk or not based on a function
- The only thing that the existing task priority does is control the existence of an additional line of text 
- We will want to be able to query a family or person's priority in PostgreSQL and not have to recreate the rules in SQL so will want to store the priority on a doc (instead of just ephemerally on a contact summary, for example).

**Some conceptual / non-visual questions:**
- What are some of the ways a person, family, or task might be considered priority?  For example… based on a risk score, danger signs, risk factors, etc… (looking for broad examples). 
- How will app developers specify a person or a family as being priority? Would this be the same as how Tasks are configured to be priority?
- The CHT doesn’t really have a defined family or family member concept… it’s more of a convention (clinic = family, for example). Do we need to prevent priority from being configured at different levels? 
- Should a family be considered `priority` if any of their family members are identified as priority? Would that be based on design guidance or enforced by the toolkit?
- Should a person be considered priority if their family is considered priority? Would that be based on design guidance or enforced by the toolkit?
- Would priority be accessible to SMS schedules?

@michaelkohn 

Most assumptions are correct however:
- Non-priority families and/or non-priority people should not receive priority tasks

For other stuff:
- Priority/risk examples: Economic vulnerability, unlikely to deliver at facility, late illness identification (@ecsalomon can add more)
- Unsure about how to specify priority but I imagine it would be the same as tasks are configured..
- There may be an instance where a clinic/nurse may need to be identified as at risk or a priority, I don't think we should make it exclusive to households only but open to more feedback/thoughts on this
- A family can be a priority as a unit without labelling every individual as priority (however if an individual is a priority, the household needs to display the priority icon for visibility on the highest level, ex. people tab)
- Priority does not seem to be accessible to SMS schedules (unless you have any suggestions on how that might work?)

To add a bit on this question:

> The CHT doesn’t really have a defined family or family member concept… it’s more of a convention (clinic = family, for example). Do we need to prevent priority from being configured at different levels?

I would say that we should support _whatever is the level displayed in the contacts list for the user_ and all levels below that (whether this is families + family members or clinics + nurses or some other combination) being priority, but not any levels above that.

With a log of locations, there are things we could do in post-hoc analysis. We might decide to exclude all second GPS locations in one analysis, or alternative to use GPS locations locked upon edit of a form only if less than half an hour has elapsed between initial submission and edit.

This change refactors how Sentinel's scheduled tasks are processed. 
Before, they were run in sequence, blocking next task until done. The 5 minute restart interval was calculated _after_ all tasks were finished. 
Now, they should run in parallel, and the scheduler checks, every 5 minutes, if a task is not already running. if not, it would start it, otherwise it would skip it and check it again next interval. 

This is pretty high risk change and should be AT-ed carefully to make sure we don't destabilize sentinel task execution. 

These are the tasks that the scheduler executes:
- due tasks - marking "scheduled" SMS tasks as "pending" so they'd be queued to be sent 
- reminders
- replications of meta dbs
- outbound
- purging
- backgroundCleanup - this is the new task that should handle deleting read docs from meta dbs and infodocs from sentinel

When AT-ing, we should make Sentinel execute all these tasks in parallel, preferably using long-running tasks, to check for potential bugs. So we need a configuration and DB setup that triggers all these actions to run at once, and possibly for a longer period of time (So the 5 minute interval overlaps with execution) and make sure we're never starting the same task twice. 

This means we need thousands of due_tasks, thousands of reminders, thousands of feedback docs to replicate from multiple user dbs to users-meta, and so on.

Ah also, when upgrading an instance to this version and start sentinel, make sure the backgroundCleanup doesn't start processing deletes from 0, but is migrated correctly and starts where `_loca/sentinel-meta-data` stopped.

On this ticket we added a new DB in CouchDB called `medic-logs`, where we add/update a document per user when they replicate docs, this document is called `replication-count-[user name]`.
The `replication-count-[user name]` contains the user name, count of replicated docs and logged date.

To test this I usually do the following requests:
1. Replicate documents with an user that has `offline` role: `GET:  /medic/_changes`
2. Get the full list of logs: `GET:  /api/v1/users-doc-count` here we should see a log with the user from 1st step. 
This endpoint has an optional query parameter, if you want to get logs of 1 user: `GET:  /api/v1/users-doc-count?user=medic` 
3.  If the count exceeds the replication limit (10.000 aprox), then when requesting to the monitor endpoint, it should return the count of users that have exceeds the limit. `GET:  /api/v1/monitoring`

The `replication-count-[user name]` will update if there is a difference between the old and the new on the following:
Log date: 1 month difference
or 
Count: 100 difference

hey @garethbowen

I think I'm done. 
I, unfortunately, had to move some code around in the Geolocation service to make the handle available to be updated by the service itself. 

The way it works is that:
-when another service requests a handle, we check if we're in the Android wrapper and call a function (`getLocationPermissions`) that will return a Boolean value, representing if we have `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` permission or not. 
-if we do (returned value is `true`) we go ahead and start the watcher and everything works exactly like before
-if we do not (returned value is `false`), we _don't_ start the watcher until we receive the trigger to do so. 
-medic-android will call a new endpoint in the AndroidApi called `locationPermissionRequestResolved`, which in turns calls a new exposed function in Geolocation service, `permissionRequestResolved`, whichs starts the watcher. 
-we don't care and don't check if the actual permission was granted. `window.navigator.geolocation` will call the `failure` callback with an error when this is the case:

```json
{
    "code": 2,
    "message": "application does not have sufficient geolocation permissions."
}
```

After a year the `userCtx` cookie would expire, and the next time the user reloads the page the webapp Session service checks for the cookie, doesn't find it, and [boots them to the login page](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.4.x/webapp/src/js/services/session.js#L73). Then the login page get route sets the `userCtx` cookie back, which the login page checks for and then redirects them back to the webapp.

- `scheduled_tasks` with null `due` dates are now set to pending based on the report `reported_date`.

This also fixes a potential problem where the "task" queue could become saturated with "errored" entries:
- for `due_tasks` these could be `scheduled_tasks` that have `message_keys` without corresponding translations (these docs are expected not to be updated). 
- for `outbound` these could be tasks that permanently fail. 

To test, 
- add 1000+ of "broken" scheduled tasks (with missing translations) + one most "recent" correct task that is valid (more recent so it'd be in the 2nd+ batch). Once the `dueTasks` task finishes, the "broken" tasks should still be `scheduled`, while the correct one should be `pending`. 
- add 1000+ of "broken" outbound tasks (with a destination that doesn't answer)  + one with "higher" uuid (so it's ordered near the end, in the 2nd batch) that has a correct destination. After `outbound` task is finished, all broken tasks should still exist, while the correct one should be "sent" and deleted.

Copying over some relevant information on why sw-precache was used and not workbox: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/5219

## swPrecache vs Workbox 
It is worth checking out the [Support Details for swPrecache](https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/sw-precache#support). TLDR: "We would recommend Workbox for new projects" but "we’ll continue to support sw-precache". 
 
Workbox looks awesome. Most notably check out [enabling offline Google Analytics](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/workbox/modules/workbox-google-analytics). So why isn't this PR using Workbox? The short answer is we probably should – but this is a big PR and Workbox is going to complicate things.  
 
Here is why I'm using the swPrecache library: 
 
1. **The community support isn't perfect for either option** - Workbox 3 supports Chrome >51, but modern [Workbox 4 only supports Chrome >56](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/workbox/releases) so really both swPrecache and latests Workbox are [both not supporting us](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bVwh8PW6r88). 
1. **Partial Precache State** - SwPrecache is pretty much exactly what we want by default: it fails to install the service worker if any resource doesn't get precached and thus the possibility of a partial precached state. Workbox delivers a best effort precache and it isn't immediately obvious to me how to best avoid a partial precache state. 
1. **Dependent Scripts** - SwPrecache inlines all dependencies directly in the service worker so we just serve one script and we are done. Workbox has a modular build which deploys dependencies along-side your service worker (~20 files). A bit messy and not a perfect fit for our build script which ends up adding twenty more attachments to the database. A quick attempt to build only the required resources ended up with some dependencies being pulled from a cdn – which is problematic for projects using domain-based data contracts.  
 
All solvable problems, but a bit of untangling to do. Imo -- the best case would be using Workbox to output a script which does exactly what swPrecache is outputting now. I'm confident we can get there if we are interested in other features of Workbox *cough* - offline google analytics - *cough*.

The specific example that Stefan was talking about is to do with the `COUCH_NODE_NAME` environment variable. We had a situation a while back where someone had their environment variable set to `x` but CouchDB was configured with the node name of `y`. This variable is infrequently used but it is used in [settings.getCredentials](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/settings/src/index.js#L31) for example. You can find documentation about the credentials management on the [docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/outbound/#credentials).

The node name is used for clustered setups but even single node CouchDB installs need this set. More about [CouchDB nodes](https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/cluster/nodes.html).

So this issue is to ensure that whatever node name environment variable is set actually exists so we can fail early with a useful error message rather than randomly down the line. Consider using the `_membership` API to check this.

An alternative approach is to remove all use of the environment variable either but auto detecting the node name on startup, or refactoring the way we store credentials ( ie: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5904 ) and the few other uses so we don't need the variable at all. This is probably outside the scope of this issue.

**+1** Axios. I used it in the past and it is simple, and works in both the browser and the server (despite we are planning for now just a replacement for scripts and backends). Furthermore:

- Axios **handles non 2xx HTTP responses as errors** (returning a rejected promise, and therefore you are able to use `try {...} catch {..}` in a _async_ function), while node-fetch no, and there is no way to create a "node-fetch" object with automatic handling of errors in certain way, you need to chain the error handler each call: https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-fetch#handling-client-and-server-errors
- Axios, like request, allows to create a [client object](https://www.npmjs.com/package/axios#creating-an-instance) where you can **define boilerplate configurations** for each request, like timeout, baseUrl, headers... with node-fetch you need to merge your base configuration with the specifics for the request each time.
Agree that Axios might be preferable in terms of migration effort, since it has an API similar enough to request-promise-native and has similar error handling capabilities.

Just a quick disclaimer to this using this approach, as it might be important for some projects. 

Server-side purging is based on user's roles, so adding a new role (even an unconfigured role) to a user will: 
a) make the server redo the purge for the role list from scratch 
b) make the user download purge doc ids from 0. The docs will have already been deleted from their device, but the user will need to download all purge ids from the server to get up to date with the new purge database.

I'd suggest that we might prioritise:

**Errors in Production** - We currently collect feedback documents which include the details of crashes and errors in production. To maintain healthy apps in production, we need to strengthen our ability to respond to these crashes and errors.  Would be great if we could 1) coalesce/group common errors/crashes, 2) send out alerts or a monthly summary of the crashes for each project, 3) since it can take time to fix issues causing crashes we likely need a list of "known" errors/crashes that should not be alerted on.

**Alerts based on telemetry data** - A list of higher-priority alerts that we might target are:  Alerts that might indicate a specific functional bug: like 1) if a task's completion rate falls to 0 or very low, or 2) if a form's completion rate falls to 0 or very low.  Or overall app health like if client-side load times for a tab or bootsrap are too high (or increase significantly).

**Comparisons** - To have actionable  telemetry data, we should be able to perform comparisons of two different production experiences. For example, how can we compare our telemetry metrics in experience A vs experience B. Where the different A/B experiences might include: cht-core upgrades, a configuration deployment, an event on the ground (like a training program).

For **Visualisation**, I don't have a prioritised list of metrics I'd start with.  This is largely useful for data exploration. To increase the discoverability of insights in telemetry data, it often needs to be sliced by user segment or visualised over time.

I have some interesting news about FF (found while trying to devise a proper title for the issue).

Not granting persistent permissions for FF (by checking the "remember this decision") does indeed only resolve one location request (the last one!).

 The reason why the assessment form hangs is because it contains an Enketo geo widget (that allows you to specify some location in the form), this widget calls `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition` and replaces the `navigator.geolocation.watchPosition` (the webapp location request) as the "last" geolocation request, that gets resolved by the user action. 

When the form doesn't have an Enketo geo widget, Firefox's behavior is exactly like Chrome's - the form will submit when you respond to the location permissions request. 
> you can click either "allow" or "block" in the request and it will successfully submit (promise resolved) for the form that's actively hung

This can be replicated using any two forms, one that doesn't have a geo widget and one that does (for example this one: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/demo-forms/geopoint.xml).

After discussing with @garethbowen it seemed as though option 3 would be preferred since we can quickly spin it up, and using flows gives more flexibility for handling multiple gateways.

I am putting notes here after exploring that further, but the summary version is that _webapp terminating_ messages can easily and reliably be handled with existing features, whereas _webapp originating_ messages have some limitations that can delay when messages get sent, and also cause duplicates to be sent.

### Webapp Terminating
Messages that are sent to the CHT can be handled by RapidPro with a simple flow that [starts with a trigger for "messages not handled anywhere else"](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/99475680-0a634380-291d-11eb-850b-0c6b8358f156.png).

The flow only needs to contain a [webhook and error handling](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/99476283-3d5a0700-291e-11eb-8fb2-c07dcf472046.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/99476330-582c7b80-291e-11eb-9752-e02367e8d885.png)

The [headers](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/99476379-76927700-291e-11eb-8a50-bb73f9186089.png), and body must be set:
```
@(json(object(
  "messages", array(
    object(
      "id", run.uuid,
      "from", replace(urns.tel,"tel:+", "+"),
      "content", results.message.value,
      "sms_sent", epoch(run.created_on),
      "sms_received", epoch(now())

    ),
  "updates", array()
  )
)))
```

Error handling could include retries, logging, and messages to the sender to let them know that their message was not processed.

### Webapp Originating

Reusing the choices from the comment above, here are the ways that messages could be sent from the CHT to people:
1. ~Write a bespoke SMS aggregator integration to Infobip~
1. **CHT-RapidPro messaging integration**: the CHT would call the [broadcast](https://textit.in/api/v2/broadcasts) API to send messages, and poll it to check the status.
    _**Pros**: no need to build or manage a RapidPro flow_ 
    _**Cons**: more involved feature in CHT yet less configurable and doesn't handle multiple RapidPro channels_
1. **CHT-outbound push to RapidPro**: A flow in RapidPro can be triggered when the state of CHT messages go to pending. 
    _**Pros**: handles multiple gateways and processing in RapidPro flows._ 
    _**Cons**: difficult to reliably trigger flow, duplicates are possible without more work_

The way the outbound push was prototyped was to trigger a flow when a message's state became `pending`. The flow would then call the SMS endpoint to get a list of _all_ messages that need to be sent, process them in small batches to send them and report the status back to the CHT. This made it easier to catch and retry any messages that failed to send previously, but makes duplicates theoretically possible if the flow was triggered multiple times before it completes and they get the same set of messages. This may have changed with recent improvements to the SMS API.

Here is what the outbound push prototype config looked like:
```
  "outbound": {
    "textit-gateway": {
      "relevant_to": "doc.type === 'data_record' && doc.tasks && doc.tasks[0] && doc.tasks[0].state && doc.tasks[0].state === 'pending'",
      "destination": {
        "base_url": "https://textit.in",
        "auth": {
          "type": "header",
          "name": "Authorization",
          "value_key": "textit.in"
        },
        "path": "/api/v2/flow_starts.json"
      },
      "mapping": {
        "flow": {
          "expr": "'abcdef1234567890'"
        },
        "urns": {
          "expr": "[ 'tel:' + doc.tasks[0].messages[0].to ]",
          "optional": false
        }
      }
    },
```
Note that the above outbound push config has limitations in that it would only trigger for the first message in `tasks`. Also, SMS schedules, which are in `scheduled_tasks`, are not being considered.

This option of triggering a flow is still advantageous since it permits more flexible channel setups, but we need the following two improvements:
- **Make sure that messages are sent without delay** perhaps by identifying (or creating) a better CHT doc trigger when there are new pending messages, and not being so dependent on the message configuration.
- **Find a reliable way to avoid duplicates** by reviewing the new SMS API behaviour, or perhaps by making the outgoing message flow non re-entrant. There is no known easy way to do this in RapidPro. One option considered in the past is to call a webhook to set and unset a semaphore in a webservice/CHT, which doesn't seem particularly robust.

Working with the team we have come up with our desired V1 and V2 solutions to address the scenarios of CHWs wanting to easily find and complete available tasks within the same household and to find tasks for households nearby. We'd like to be able to (V1) sort and group tasks and (V2) to add an interstitial page once a task is submitted to prompt users to complete other tasks within that group. For this issue I'll focus on V1: - Default sort by due date as this is how CHWs prioritize their work - Dropdown sort selection to view task groups (in this example, by household and "general" for tasks that are not associated to a household) - Groups are labelled and ordered numerically for days left and alphabetically for households - Tasks within groups are ordered by due date (ex. within household A, show tasks that are due soonest) - Once a task is submitted, return to the same sort order - If the user leaves the task tab (ex. closes app, opens other tab) and returns to it, default to due date view The third screen (priority) is an example of how this pattern might scale to include future sorting options. Questions: cc @garethbowen - If we are collecting GPS data are we able to sort by household task distance? ex. within 2km, 5km+? This might be a more efficient way to find nearby tasks than scrolling through names - This specific issue refers to households but I'm wondering if we are able to make these groups configurable so that other non-household apps may utilize this feature in a way to better suit? - Can this address https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5997? As always, let me know if I missed anything ✌️

> If we are collecting GPS data are we able to sort by household task distance? ex. within 2km, 5km+? This might be a more efficient way to find nearby tasks than scrolling through names

This is definitely an idea worth exploring but I think it's probably outside the scope of this issue. Currently the GPS is collected based on where the form was filled in which isn't always at the family home. I think to do this properly we would want to add a location widget to the family registration to explicitly set the location of the family home. It may also be technically challenging to work how out far apart two GPS coordinates are, so I wouldn't like to see that derail the other improvements in this issue.

> This specific issue refers to households but I'm wondering if we are able to make these groups configurable so that other non-household apps may utilize this feature in a way to better suit?

Because contact types are configurable the system doesn't know which type is a "household". I imagined that the implementation would be something like "allow sorting by the lowest place contact type you can see". Depending on how the replication depth is configured this may be useful for supervisors to group based on clinics.

> Can this address #5997?

I think that can be done separately by adding an additional filter option to this filter.

> Very curious about the interface being exposed to app developers. Sounds like we can define groups, assign tasks into one or more groups with an associated sortable key?

Currently I don't see that specified in the design. As in my comments above my initial thought was to implement this based on the configured contact types. I'd prefer that we implement a few hardcoded filters (eg: date, contact, priority) and if necessary allow them to be toggled on and off, with a configurable default. This allows the Product team to regression test pre-release and optimise the performance of each filter.

> The default proposed here is "no grouping" (sort by due date) - could app builders select the default

The concern with setting the default sorting by contact group is that tasks for the Yankovic family will always be at the bottom, so even overdue tasks will probably be missed. So I don't think that sorting by contact group should ever be the default.

> ...two apps right now would want the "priority" grouping by default

Priority sorting is covered by [a separate issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5997) so it would be good to flag these projects there to help with the design of that feature.

Some context re: EBS

Data can be pushed to different 'silos' within DHIS. Our current integration approach focusses on **datasets** which store summarised values per time period.

For EBS, MoH's initial idea was to track more transactional data via events which can then be summaries as reports using DHIS' analytics framework. This poses one challenge as we will be pushing data multiple times for each signal as it moves through reporting, triaging, verification, investigation etc. This means we'll need to keep track of an identifier on our end that can be used to update the original submission on our end.

Currently outbound is a one-way street and we have no way to being able to pull any information, let alone use that new information and update records on our end.

If we are to rely on aggregation client side, MoH would have an added cost of subsidising data costs for the users.

I didn't catch if this is a production or development instance.  If it's a development instance, we recommend using either a tool like [ngrok](https://pagekite.net/) or [pagekite](https://ngrok.com/) to expose your instance to the internet.  These services give you a public URL which does SSL termination. These are ephemeral though - the external URL to access the instance will change.  

We've also JUST published a guide I wrote about a [self hosted solution to share your dev instance](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/debugging/secure-sharing-of-developer-instance/). [Wireguard](https://golb.hplar.ch/2019/01/expose-server-vpn.html) is another solution that comes to mind. This, again, is still dependent on an external linux server.

As an aside, I believe you could simplify the demands on your users by mapping external docker host port 443 to internal port 5988. Having a local server replicate the data from the primary installation is something we've given quite a lot of thought to. There are some potential challenges to this approach.

1. There are certain actions in API and Sentinel services that should be only performed once per dataset and with this concept they will be executed on every facility device. This will cause performance issues and Document Update Conflicts in the database. We have [this issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5563) tracking an idea for "secondary" or "satellite" servers which would work to resolve this problem.
2. If the power goes out at a facility then the secondary server will be unavailable. This can be made more resilient with a UPS system for the server and WiFi router so phones will still have access. Another possibility is implementing a feature in CHT so the devices can fall back to replicating directly to the cloud server if the local server is unavailable.
3. Securing the 1000s of secondary servers is a difficult challenge. To protect the health information stored in couchdb each server would need to be stored in a locked room with an encrypted device which is operationally very difficult to implement.
4. Offline storage requires an HTTPS connection so to use the devices in offline mode you'll need to solve the certificate challenge. This is a browser limitation and not something we can easily get around. This could be solved with a self-signed certificate which is manually added to each device, or perhaps a wildcard certificate so each facility can have its own subdomain.

> Is there a way to generate SSL certificates for LAN addresses? I have researched but I can't seem to get any leads. Any guidance will really be appreciated.

@ojwanganto @andrineM @makombe: Inherently, there is nothing that ties an SSL certificate to a specific IP address.  That is, if you generate a certificate on a server with a public IP address, you can use this certificate on any server with any IP address.  The one thing that must be true, is that the [HTTP request's hostname](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Host) must match the certificate's [common name (CN)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_key_certificate#Types_of_certificate). 

The way we tie an IP to a hostname is, of course, through DNS.  There is no rule against having a domain resolve to different IP addresses in different locations. This is called [split horizon DNS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split-horizon_DNS).

When we take all this in to considerations, one way (of many!) to solve your problem might look like this:

1. Purchase a certificate for https://your-deployment-site.com .  This should expire in 1 year.  You will need to prove you own the domain via the [domain-validation process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain-validated_certificate).
2. Taking care to protect the [private key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public-key_cryptography), copy the certificate and private key for https://your-deployment-site.com to each of your 1000 locations.
3. At each location, run a simple DNS server that resolves https://your-deployment-site.com to which ever static, [private IP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RFC1918) you CHT server is on. While this can be different in each location, there's no reason you can't make these all the same (eg 192.168.1.100) at all locations.
4. When any client connects to the LAN, either desktop via ethernet or mobile devices via WiFI, have your DHCP server tell network clients to use your local DNS server.
5. When these clients request https://your-deployment-site.com, your local DNS server will resolve it to the local IP at that physical location (again eg 192.168.1.100). 
6. Given the HTTP request's `host` matches the `CN` in the certification, the `https://` connection will be valid and enabled

This will allow the same SSL certificate exist in many locations and be used by many web servers. You could also use a wildcard cert to enable each location to have a different name.  This might come in handy if you ever expect a device from location A to keep from syncing when at location B (eg `https;//locaitonA.your-deployment-site.com` vs `https;//locaitonB.your-deployment-site.com`)

**Note** -  [1 year is the longest](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/mozilla-reduces-tls-certificate-lifespan-to-1-year-in-september/) a cert may exist and this may get shorter! We strongly recommend designing an automated process to keep your 1000 locations updated. 

You're likely already working on a prototype to prove this can all work in a custom, non automated way offline. For the local, offline DNS server, something like [Pi-Hole](https://pi-hole.net/) or [dnsgui](https://github.com/kroy-the-rabbit/dnsgui) (vs a more [heavy solution](https://www.slashroot.in/how-to-configure-split-horizon-dns-in-bind)) with a GUI can be used to create your custom domain entry on the offline LAN.  You will need a public DNS entry to create the cert so, as @Hareet  suggested, you can use [Duck DNS](http://www.duckdns.org/).  If you don't have a public server to point your DNS entry to, I recommend provisioning a cheap [$5 USD/month server](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/) and using a [Let's Encrypt free certificate](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-secure-apache-with-let-s-encrypt-on-ubuntu-18-04), also as @Hareet  suggested. I see Digital Ocean also offers [free DNS](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/) if you're paying for something like a droplet already.

Once Let's Encrypt generates the certificate and private key, you can copy this down to your offline LAN CHT test server. With your offline DNS server in place resolving your test domain to a local IP on the LAN where CHT is installed, it should work!

See [this post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10079707/https-connection-using-curl-from-command-line) and [this post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/20983217/how-to-display-the-subject-alternative-name-of-a-certificate) respectively with some examples. 
2. You're using a sub-sub-domain.  Not likely, but be sure you using just subdomain (`*.domain.com`).  You can't use a sub-subdomain ( `*.*.domain.com`) with a wildcard certificate.
3. You don't have the full certificate chain set up correctly.  Often certifcates come with 3 files: the public certificate, the private key and the intermediate certificate. In `nginx` for example, they specify you need `cat` them together.  See their [documentation about chains](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/configuring_https_servers.html#chains). 
4. While most modern CA's will give you a widely compatible certificate, you may have one that does not work with all devices. This [SE post](https://android.stackexchange.com/questions/26500/what-trusted-root-cas-are-included-in-android-by-default) has some good info on this.

Some general tips that might be helpful:
* Start with the simplest set up possible and build up complexity from there.  In your case, that might be an Ubuntu 16 server with nginx and your wildcard cert serving a single static page.  
* Every difference is an opportunity for something to break.  If your fully online, public server works - what is difference to your offline server?  
* Test the same way every time.  Be sure you have documented test steps for each server configuration you try.  This way you can be sure, for example, you avoid hitting the [CHT bug](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6479) I mention above. 
* Record all error messages.  Error messages will give you a strong indication of what is wrong and give you a good search string to use to find others who may have solved the problem
* Consider [hooking up a phone so you can remotely debug the browser](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/chrome-devtools/remote-debugging/).  This may give you more info to go on per my prior point.

It sounds like you're close! Because you're needing to update the `/etc/hosts` file, it sounds like the issue is that your LAN clients are not seeing the Pi-hole DNS server  or that the Pi-hole is not working correctly.  I would:
* Be sure your DHCP server is set to use the Pi-Hole as DNS.  You can read more about this on Pi-hole's docs [here](https://discourse.pi-hole.net/t/how-do-i-configure-my-devices-to-use-pi-hole-as-their-dns-server/245) and [here](https://discourse.pi-hole.net/t/how-do-i-configure-my-devices-to-use-pi-hole-as-their-dns-server/245).  Basically, when the DHCP server gives the client an IP on the LAN, along with what the gateway and netmask is, it also informs the client which DNS server to use.
* Make sure your Pi-hole is configured to give the correct responses.  You can test DNS queries using the `dig` command line utility.  [Read more about it here](https://phoenixnap.com/kb/linux-dig-command-examples), but idea is you can query your Pi-hole manually. So if your Pi-Hole was at `10.0.0.1` and your cht instances was at `cht.domain.com`, you would run the command: `dig +short @10.0.0.1 cht.domain.com`.  If you get back nothing, there is something wrong with your Pi-Hole.  If you get back the IP address behind `cht.domain.com`, the Pi-hole is configured correctly.
* To test your DHCP is set up to hand out the Pi-hole as the DNS server, you can leave off the `@10.0.0.1` part of the `dig` command.  This will tell your client to use the default DNS serve (the Pi-hole).  That would look like:  `dig +short cht.domain.com`

If you get DHCP set up correct, confirm all this with `dig`, you should not only be able to remove all `/etc/hosts` entries, but all devices on the LAN, including phones, should just work with no further configuration.  

NB - be sure to remove `/etc/hosts` entries!  These can override DNS settings and cause a lot of confusion when configuring DNS.

So I dug into this, I checked the logs of the fluentd daemonset on the node where gamma-dev resides and found this error appearing so often in the logs. `Worker 0 finished unexpectedly with signal SIGKILL`.  I discovered that when we were deploying the k8s daemon set, we set the memory limit to 200Mi. Now the fluentd flush buffer on the node labeled `testing` was hiting the memory limit and K8s was actively killing all fluent threads with a SIGKILL . This meant that fluent was not pushing logs to elastic. All the gamma pods reside on this node . All other pods on this node did not have logs in elastic search. 


 I have grown the memory limit to 400Mi , also reduced the size of the flush buffer and deployed new fluentd daemon sets across all nodes in our cluster.  I have monitored them and I see that  k8s is no longer actively killing workers. I will keep monitoring  for about 24 hours to see if we still have this pod memory pressure issue.  I can also see logs from  all pods on the testing node showing up in  kibana. 

So to calculate the buffer size you need to need to to look at this config section of the fluent configmap

```yaml
<buffer tag, time>
            flush_mode interval
            timekey 1h
            flush_thread_count 8
            flush_interval 10s
            chunk_limit_size 1MB
            queue_limit_length 16
            retry_max_interval 30
            retry_forever true
        </buffer>

```
Buffer size=flush_thread_count X chunk_limit_size X queue_limit_length

The memory limits are set in the daemonset config
```yaml
   resources:
          limits:
            memory: 400Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 400Mi

```

@antonykhaemba  - thanks for passing along the @chesterosoronyas's concerns!

Generally speaking, an ideal situation would be where every deployment is identical in its configuration and hardware. This would make trouble shooting easier as you could document the single way every site is configured and anyone with the documentation could know how it works. This would include how you resolve DNS at each location.  This is good to keep in mind while we work to resolve this!

However, the real world often isn't an ideal situation, so let me try and address your concerns:

>  My concern is what about a scenario where the internet connection is based on use of modem 

I'm not quite sure what this means.  Maybe it means that the there is no router such that the cable or DSL modem from the ISP in the facility is directly connected to only one computer? 

If this one computer is the ubuntu box with your CHT instance on it, you need to figure a way to get other devices to talk to the CHT instance.  That might look like:
* adding a 2nd physical NIC to the CHT instance so it can talk to a LAN where a DHCP server and WiFi access points live so that laptops/desktop/mobiles can talk to it over that LAN
* disconnecting the CHT instance's NIC from the modem and connecting it to a LAN where it can talk other devices. This is clearly not ideal because it needs to be physically moved every time, but may work as stop gap solution if locations are hard to get to or you're budget constrained.

If the CHT server is not directly connected to the modem, the solution below may work.

> or one does not have any access to any router configuration in the network how will you enable the server accessible in such scenarios

Pi-Hole actually comes with it's [own DHCP server](https://discourse.pi-hole.net/t/how-do-i-use-pi-holes-built-in-dhcp-server-and-why-would-i-want-to/3026). Given you said you had a computer running Pi-hole already, one solution might be to turn off the DHCP server on the router and turn it on Pi-hole. The Pi-Hole DHCP server will of course tell clients to use Pi-Hole for DNS.

However, turning off the DHCP server on the router does mean you're actually making a change to the router configuration.  You said you you might not have any access to the router configuration.  Another solution, which does mean re-using hardware or possibly purchasing new hardware, would be to set up a new LAN that has:
* CHT server
* Pi-Hole instance
* WiFi Access point 
* Ethernet switch connecting Pi-Hole, CHT and any other clients

To reduce the need to purchase or gather additional hardware, you could actually run Pi-Hole in another docker container on the same Ubuntu box where the CHT is running.  To further minimize the extra hardware needed, you could even run the WiFi access point on the CHT instance as well, using  [built in features to 16.04](https://websiteforstudents.com/creating-wireless-hotspot-on-ubuntu-16-04-18-04-lts/?PageSpeed=noscript).

This last solution could done intentionally at every location to standardize your deployment where the CHT server has as much of the software all in one place (docker, CHT, Pi-Hole, and WiFI AP).

> 2. If no `locale` cookie is set, use the browser default. This is passed in the request's accept-language header. This may not match with the two letter code that we use so make a best effort here. Furthermore it may not match one of the supported languages for this project.
> 3. If the browser default doesn't match any supported language, use the project "default application language" set in configuration.
> 4. If the "default application language" in the project config isn't set (very unlikely), default to English.

Thinking on this some more, a really good UX would be to have a CHT instance be able to set a self expire date and a hand off URL.  That is, if we ship a branded for a deployment, it could be pointing to test.server.com.   However, when ever we want, we can tell test.server.com to tell clients on XYZ date to start using prod.server.com and that the app will reset to this URL on XYZ date.

This avoids the problem of CHWs using the unbranded app for testing and then being expected to remember to stop using it on a certain time.  Instead, they'd have just one app that just did the right thing them.

Further, the URL could be cached so that the transition could A) happen offline and B) not send any more traffic to test.server.com once the cut over has happened. In the worst case an app would get reset, contact test.server.com and be immediately told to go to prod.server.com.

Not quite sure how we'd handle authentication unless they had identical accounts on both servers.  And of course, I have no idea how hard this would be with in the app itself - this is a wild brainstorming scenario ;)

The muting transition already doesn't run if the main contact (the muting/unmuting report's subject) is already in the correct state: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/muting.js#L121
(we even have an event and an e2e test that checks that a muted contact is not updated if it's already muted: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/e2e/sentinel/transitions/muting.spec.js#L382)

but if it's not (which is the case here, where the transitions run on two servers at once ... ) and the muting/unmuting cascade starts (where descendants or ancestors are updated), indeed the code just updates regardless of current state: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/0280e8caa08a2b7c65958b30d2ee8eb9dc1f7d60/shared-libs/transitions/src/lib/muting_utils.js#L58
So this is the place to change.

I'm also sharing a comment I made on the Slack thread: 

If it's a race condition, where the muting report is replicated before the family (makes sense if it would be "first" in the changes feed), you might still be in this situation, even with this code change, because at the time where the second sentinel runs on the report, the family would not be muted on that server, because it wasn't replicated yet. 

You can even see proof of this, where the rev number is the same on both docs: 

1. both servers have the family are on rev 5
2. muting report happens
3. server1's sentinel processes the muting report and the family gets rev 6
4. replication starts
5. server2 receives the report
6. server2's sentinel processes the muting report and the family gets rev 6
7. replication reaches the family document
8. CONFLICT and both docs are on rev 6

If indeed the report was "updated" (re-muted) after replication, you'd see the family on server 2 be on rev 7.

It's not the case @dianabarsan. In my case I have 3 instances, `LG mainstream` (3.6.0), `CIHA` (3.9.0) and `all-data` (3.6.0). `All-data` combines data from the two.
- Replication between `mainstream` and `CIHA` is as follows:
   - `mainstream` to `CIHA` is coninuous filtered by 20 CHW areas
   - `CIHA` to `mainstream` is continuous filtered by a set of reports e.g. muting, so that supervisors can verify for actual contact muting to happen. Supervisors are on `mainstream`.
- Replication between `mainstream`/`ciha` and `all-data`
   - `mainstream` to `all-data` is continuous, not filtered.
   - `ciha` to `all-data` is continuous filtered by doc types contacts and data_records.

##### That said,
- The update to muting date happens from `mainstream` to `CIHA`, on already muted contacts
   - This means we always have to deal with conflicts in `all-data`, which feeds into Klipfolio dashboards and causes discrepancies in indicators vs in-app analytics (CHWs are using CIHA).
   - The discrepancy can be explained in that the muted attribute gets excluded in the latest revision of the doc in `all-data`, meaning that some contacts muted in `mainstream` and `ciha` end up getting unmuted in `all-data`.

Happy to do a call to further clarify using some affected documents.

Does the muting transition have to run on all instances? Can't you just keep the muting transition enabled on one instance alone? 
With continuous replication, there's a chance that both instances receive and process the muting report at the same time, causing the conflicts. The only way to guarantee no conflicts is to only run muting on one instance - the one that has all contacts (that doesn't get contact documents filtered from other instances).

Another solution, if you absolutely need all / both servers to run muting, is to have different muting forms per server, and update the muting transition config so one server doesn't run muting on the same forms as the other.

        model.children.forEach(child => {

I pushed two more commits
- one to consolidate the "RapidPro" name (and never using a dash between rapid and pro). 
- one to handle rate limiting when polling (backing off when rate limiting is triggered). 

About rate limiting: 
- it's the standard Django rate limiting
- number of requests is per endpoint
- requesting after limit is reached doesn't do anything, except fail the request
- the `retry-after` is useless. it returns a rough idea of when the next opening spot for one request will come. For our endpoint, if the limit is reached, the maximum retry-after is 60 seconds, which is exactly the interval at which we request again.

cht-core-starter also allows devs to move easily between applications without 10-15 minutes of transitional setup. this is very useful for us because one dev might work on 1-4 different cht applications.

What I think is happening is caused by us proxying stuff to CouchDB when no other API endpoints "match" the request. 
When the request has a body that is large enough, and Couch processes the request without waiting for the body to be entirely received and responds with something (in the cases above, a 404).

and try to add our headers and content on top of what Couch responded: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/server-utils.js#L33

It's probably some race condition in some node internals, since it only happens on POST requests (where something could still be streaming data) and not on GET requests for example.

It looks like you have some sort of a bad merge, since your diff lists code that already exists in `master` (not to mention that there are 500 changed files and 40k lines of changes). 
Also, I'm noticing you're actually committing the entire medic-conf source code in `/config/default/medic-conf`. Is this intended? Isn't `medic-conf` already a dependency for the default config? How should we maintain this copy of medic-conf?

> Is there any possibility that medic-conf would one-day get a frontend and not just be a CLI tool? In general, the concept of moving GUI components of the admin console from the cht-core into a frontend for medic-conf has been discussed. If this is a possibility, then potentially cht-cli is not a great name for that repo.

Taking this into account, a safe option would be `cht-conf`, and having `cht` as the app name in command line. 

Going with `cht-conf` or `cht-cli` seems to depend on whether the primary purpose of the tool is to manage CHT instances, or if it is to mange/use the CHT via command line. Right now it is being considered for both, since you can upload/download config, but you can also add messages.

From my perspective either is more appropriate than `medic-conf`, and if `cht-conf` is less disruptive or confusing, let's go with that.

_**Update**: After a quick poll, the decision is to go with the overwhelming favourite of `cht-conf`_
